pie: ǵérh₂onts h₂yuHn̥ḱósyo h₂nr̥bʰós h₂roh₁dʰéyet. h₁yód deywós h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént téḱnom h₁ésm̥. gʰrómom péh₂wr̥-kʷe memónh₂e. dyḗws kr̥snós h₁ést h₂énh₁mos-kʷe gʰrémet. dómes tr̥mént dóruh₂-kʷe péth₁t. nu soksóybʰos gʷm̥sḱónth₂ wédōr widóm. déh₂nu tékʷome ph₃mé-kʷe méh₂teres-kʷe nos sméyn̥t. h₂yúHn̥ḱōs wos téḱnoybʰos ḱód spélom wr̥h₁té.
english: An old man spoke to the young men. "When the god slew the serpent, I was a child. I remember the thunder and the fire. The sky was black, and the wind roared. The houses trembled, and the trees fell. Then I saw the waters coming down from the rocks. We ran to the river and drank, and our mothers laughed. Tell this story to your children, young ones!"

pie: ń̥dʰgʷʰitom deywósyo ḱléwos. méǵh₂ h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ h₁ludʰéy. nu h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént wédōr-kʷe spért. h₂néres ḱlutóm h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ gʷéHyete. h₁ésyo-ge wékʷesh₂ h₁sn̥tyéh₂. nu h₁ésyo ḱléwos méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t.
english: Imperishable is the fame of the god. Great is his name among the people. Then he slew the serpent, and he freed the waters. Men, sing his famous name! His words are indeed true. Now may his fame be great.

english: From inside the rock the waters cried: "Hero, free us!" Of-Goodly-Fame heard their voice and asked: "Who holds you?" "An ill-minded serpent holds us in the rock." He broke it and went in. Inside, the hollow was dark. There he found it lying asleep. He cut off its head, and it did not wake. They came out and said: "You freed us; your fame will be great."

pie: suHnús gʰrómom ḱléwt bʰéyh₂t-kʷe. ph₂térm̥ prḗḱst kʷíd dyḗws stonh₂éyeti. ph₂tḗr wéwket pérkʷunos h₁ógʷʰim h₂ḱm̥néh₁ gʷʰn̥sḱéti. wédōr h₂ew gʷm̥sḱéti deywós-kʷe h₁ím h₂ew gʷʰn̥sḱéti. mē tréses pós h₂wérst. nu h₂wérst suHnús-kʷe ḱlush₁yét. h₂éǵrōs ǵʰelh₃wṓs h₂éyeri h₁sént. ne bʰéyh₂t swépt-kʷe.
english: A son heard the thunder and was afraid. He asked his father: "Why does the sky thunder?" The father said: "Perkwunos strikes the serpent with the stone. It comes back to the waters, and the god strikes it again. Do not fear: afterwards it rains." Then it rained, and the son listened. In the morning the fields were green. He was not afraid, and he slept.

pie: pérkʷune h₂éngʷʰim h₂ḱm̥néh₁ téwks. ísh₁re nos póyḱons tukdʰí. nu nos gʷṓs téḱneh₂-kʷe ph₂sdʰí. h₁uséwōm-ge nos déh₃tor ḱléwos dh₃dʰí. h₂éḱmō toy h₁íns próti péth₂oyh₁t. kh₂n̥mń̥bʰis te gʷr̥néHomes.
english: Perkwunos, you struck the snake with the stone. Strike our enemies, strong one! Guard our cows and our children! Giver of good things, give us fame indeed! May your stone fly against them! We shall praise you with songs.

pie: h₁ógʷʰis h₂ékʷeh₂su péri ḱéyo. deywṓs h₁ím widónt h₁ésmōd-kʷe trésont. dyḗm upó bʰugént n̥bʰróysu-kʷe Hn̥dʰí ḱélonto. gʰrómosyo somHós dʰéh₁s dʰérst. h₁éymos wéwket mē trésete. h₁ógʷʰim moréyōh₂. h₂én h₁r̥sḱét h₁ím-kʷe h₂ḱm̥néh₁ trís kélh₂t. h₁ésyo h₁orséh₂ trémt nu mért. deywṓs h₂ew ní gʷmént n̥ḱéwi-kʷe péri sth₂ént. h₁ím gʷr̥nHént h₁yós dʰérst.
english: The serpent lay around the waters. The gods saw it and trembled before it. They fled up to the sky and hid under the clouds. The god of thunder alone took courage. He said to them: "Do not tremble! I shall kill the serpent." He went there and struck it three times with the stone. Its tail shook, and then it died. The gods came down again and stood around the dead one. They praised him, the one who had dared.

pie: h₂ówis h₁éḱwōskʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁e h₁ógʷʰim próti stéygʰetām. h₁óynos bʰéyh₂t h₁éteros dʰérst. h₁yós dʰérst só h₁ím ǵʰoysóh₁ h₁néǵʰt. ǵʰwḗr mért wédōr-kʷe soksṓd h₁éǵʰs h₁éyt. bʰréh₂tēr dṓm drémt h₁yós bʰéyh₂t h₁ludʰíbʰos-kʷe wéwket. bʰréh₂tēr moy ǵʰwḗrm̥ wént h₁ím sepelyéte. h₁éysōm ǵérh₂onts ph₂tḗr mówdoh₁ smḗyt. h₁léwdʰeyes bʰréh₂term̥ sepelyónt h₁ésmey-kʷe kʷékʷlom yugóm-kʷe dh₃ént.
english: Two brothers went out against the serpent. The one was afraid; the other took courage. He who took courage stabbed it with a spear. The beast died, and the waters went out from the rock. The brother who had been afraid ran home and said to the people: "My brother slew the beast; praise him!" Their old father laughed with joy. The people honored the brother and gave him a wheel and a yoke.

pie: h₂nr̥ménēs póyḱom próti h₁éyt. h₁ím ǵʰoysóh₁ pért ne-kʷe mért. h₁ím dwís pért gʰrémet-kʷe. h₁ím trís pért h₁ésyo-kʷe ḱérh₂sō bʰindtó. h₁ésyo h₁ésh₂r̥ kr̥snóm h₁ést. h₁ésh₂r̥ h₁ésmōd h₁éǵʰs tékʷet wédesh₂-kʷe h₁sh₂énh₁ ḱóm tékʷet. srówōs ḱórkās léwh₃ont dóruh₂-kʷe píph₃et. h₂nr̥ménēs stéh₂t swóm-kʷe ǵʰoysóm tl̥néh₂t. tewh₂téh₂ h₁ím kʷéḱt ḱlutóm-kʷe h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ gʷr̥néHt.
english: Man-Minded went against the enemy. He struck it once with a spear, and it did not die. He struck it twice, and it roared. He struck it three times, and its head split. Its blood was black. Blood ran out of it, and with the blood the waters ran. The streams washed the pebbles, and the trees drank. Man-Minded stood up and lifted his spear. The tribe saw him and praised his famous name.

pie: deywṓs ḱóm sdént. h₁óynos h₂éǵt kʷós h₁ógʷʰim moréyēti. ne kʷis wéwket h₁éysōm ḱérdh₂ h₂énǵʰesh₁ trémt. nu pérkʷunos stéh₂t wéwket-kʷe h₁éyoh₂. swóns HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons yéwgt. deywṓs h₁ím wl̥h₁ént h₁ésmey-kʷe h₂éḱmonm̥ dh₃ént. ph₂tḗr dyḗws h₂éǵt súHnew moy h₁idʰí pr̥dʰí-kʷe. h₁éyt h₁ím-kʷe pért mért-kʷe. nu h₁ím sepelyónt.
english: The gods sat together. One said: "Who will slay the serpent?" No one answered; their hearts trembled with fear. Then Perkwunos stood up and said: "I shall go." He yoked his swift horses. The gods chose him and gave him the stone. Father Sky said: "Go, my son, and strike!" He went and struck it, and it died. Then they honored him.

pie: pérkʷune te ísh₁re ǵʰuHéyomes. dh₂pnóm-ge nos gʷm̥dʰí h₁yós h₁ógʷʰim kélh₂s. sweh₂dú-ge médʰu ph₃dʰí h₁yód toy ǵʰumé. wéyHm̥-ge nos méǵh₂-kʷe ḱléwos dh₃dʰí. póyḱons téwe h₂ḱm̥néh₁ gʷl̥h₁dʰí.
english: Perkwunos, strong one, we call upon you. Come indeed to our feast, you who struck the serpent! Drink indeed the sweet mead that we have poured for you! Give us indeed strength and great fame! Strike the enemies with your stone!

pie: tat kukruwants awis agram ā bʰugat.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: pérkʷune te ḱúh₁re déywe gʷr̥nHmés. dusménesm̥-ge h₁ógʷʰim péruni gʷʰéns. h₁yós h₂ékʷās spérs n̥smé gʷm̥dʰí. h₁yós soksóm bʰéyds téwe nos wéyHm̥ dh₃dʰí. ḱléwos toy h₂nr̥sú ń̥dʰgʷʰitom. nu toy sóǵʰos h₂r̥Hmós lewkóm-kʷe toy h₃ókʷ. h₁erkʷóm nos ḱludʰí n̥sméy-kʷe priHós h₁sdʰí.
english: Perkwunos, strong god, we praise you. You indeed slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain. You who freed the waters, come to us! You who split the rock, give us your strength! Your fame among men is imperishable. Now mighty is your arm, and bright your eye. Hear our hymn, and be dear to us!

pie: h₂éngʷʰis dʰéh₁sm̥ dʰréwgʰt. sh₂wéni légʰet smḗyt-kʷe. sékʷt wédos méǵʰye ne h₁ésti h₂ékʷeh₂es h₂epó lelikʷḗr. déywe h₂epó gʷéh₂t. h₂éǵrōs h₂sowsṓs h₁sént tewh₂téh₂-kʷe HréwdHt. dʰéh₁s dʰrówgʰom kʷéḱt gʰrémet-kʷe. h₂ew gʷémt h₁ím-kʷe gʷr̥h₂úh₁ h₂ḱm̥néh₁ dʰéwgʰt. h₁ésyo h₃ésth₁h₂ Hrunépt wódr̥-kʷe h₁éǵʰs tékʷet. h₁ésyo dʰrówgʰos h₁ím ne spért. h₁ésyo krépos ḱórkeh₂su légʰet tewh₂téh₂-kʷe wódr̥ píph₃et.
english: The snake deceived the god. It lay in the sun and laughed. It said: "I have no water; the waters have gone away." The god went away. But the fields were dry, and the tribe cried out. The god saw the lie and grew angry. He came back and struck it with the heavy stone. He broke its bones, and the water ran out. Its lie did not save it. Its body lay on the pebbles, and the tribe drank the water.

pie: gʷHrēi owis, kʷesyo wl̥Hnā ne ēst, eḱwōns espeḱet, oinom gʰe gʷr̥um woǵʰom weǵʰontm̥, oinomkʷe meǵam bʰorom, oinomkʷe ǵʰm̥enm̥ ōḱu bʰerontm̥.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: bʰáge te h₁uséwōm déh₃tor gʷr̥nHmés. nu nos wédōr déh₂nuh₂-kʷe sélǵs. gʷówes nos wédos píph₃onti. téḱneh₂-ge nos gʷíh₃weti lóygeti-kʷe. ísh₁re-ge tébʰye h₁erkʷóm gʷéHyomes. h₁wésew nos ḱérdh₂ twéd mudréh₂. n̥sméy priHós h₁sdʰí h₁wésuh₂-kʷe nos dh₃dʰí.
english: God, giver of good things, we praise you. Then you set free the waters and the rivers for us. Our cattle drink the water. Our children indeed live and play. Strong one, we sing indeed a hymn to you. Our hearts are glad because of you, good one. Be dear to us, and give us good things!

pie: téḱnom h₂éwh₂om prḗḱst. kʷós h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént. ǵérh₂onts sékʷt. gʰrómosyo dʰéh₁s tewh₂sós h₁ím gʷʰént. h₁ím h₂ḱm̥néh₁ diwés gʷélh₁t. kʷíd h₁ím gʷélh₁t. wédōr Hwért h₂néres-kʷe tr̥syónt. h₁ésyo dénḱtreh₂ dl̥h₁gʰéh₂ h₁ést h₁ésyo-kʷe h₃ókʷih₁ h₁rudʰróyh₁ h₁stā́m. nu wédōr sréweti píph₃omes-kʷe. téḱnom smḗyt dṓm-kʷe drémt.
english: A child asked its grandfather: "Who slew the serpent?" The old man said: "The god of thunder slew it, the strong one. He hit it with a stone from the sky." "Why did he hit it?" "It had shut in the waters, and men were thirsty. Its fangs were long, and its eyes were red. Now the waters flow, and we drink." The child laughed and ran home.

pie: dʰugh₂tḗr méh₂term̥ wékʷsperoy prḗḱst nu kúdʰe h₁ógʷʰis ḱéyor. sokʷéyet bʰágos h₁ím sh₂imń̥bʰis mréy Hn̥dʰí bʰéndʰet. h₂ew gʷémeti. h₁yód gʷémeti h₁ím h₂ew téwketi. bʰéwdʰeti h₂lékseti-kʷe nos. mē troméyes ssdʰí. dʰugh₂tḗr h₂énh₁mom ḱléwt. h₂stéres démi upér luként. dʰugh₂tḗr légʰt swépt-kʷe.
english: At evening a daughter asked her mother: "Where does the serpent lie now?" She said: "The god bound it with ropes beneath the sea." "Will it come back?" "If it comes, he will strike it again. He is awake, and he protects us. Do not be afraid; rest!" The daughter heard the wind. Above the house the stars shone. The daughter lay down and slept.

pie: h₁ógʷʰim-ge téwkt wédōr-kʷe spért. nu soksóm gʷr̥h₂úh₁ h₂ḱm̥néh₁ bʰéydt. gʷṓs péruns h₂ewlṓd h₁éǵʰs wédʰet. sóh₂wl̥ h₂ew dʰǵʰémi upér léwkt. nu tóm gʷr̥nHmés nu tóm ǵʰuHéyomes. nu h₁ésmey stuh₂rṓy séngʷʰōmes.
english: He struck the serpent, and he freed the waters. He split the rock with the heavy stone. He led the cows out of the hollow of the rock. The sun grew bright again over the earth. Him we praise now; him we call upon. Let us sing to him, the strong one!

pie: nu h₁léwdʰereh₂es h₂ékʷeh₂es sréwete. nu wos ish₁rós h₂n̥gʷʰéys spért. gʷṓs nos h₂ówins-kʷe h₂élete. h₂ékʷeh₂es nos méh₂teres h₁wésuh₂ dh₃té. h₂éǵrons-ge nos wos wédesh₁ pl̥nh₁té. nu-kʷe yúH sweh₂déwih₂es lewkéh₂es-kʷe.
english: Free waters, flow now! Then the strong one freed you from the snake. You nourish our cattle and our sheep. Waters, mothers, give us good things! Fill our fields indeed with your water! And now you are sweet and bright.

pie: h₂éngʷʰis dʰubʰróy h₂ewlóy dʰǵʰémi Hn̥dʰí ḱéyo. léwks h₂én ne h₁ést. déh₂n̥wōm srówons h₃dn̥tsú dʰoréyet. deywóḱlewēs h₂ewlóm h₁n̥dó ní h₁éyt. péh₂wr̥ swóy ǵʰóstoy bʰéret. péh₂wr̥ kʷéḱt bʰéyh₂t-kʷe. srówons léh₁t bʰéwgt-kʷe. wiHrós h₁ím sékʷeto h₁ím-kʷe kr̥snóy wédesi moréyowe. pl̥h₁uyéh₂ōm h₂éwyōm h₃ésth₁h₂ h₂ewlóy légʰet. déh₂nuh₂ úd h₂éǵroysu upér sréwet. nu wiHrós sóh₂wl̥ upó h₁ludʰét. h₁ésyo méh₂tēr h₁ím kʷéḱt mówdoh₁-kʷe HréwdHt.
english: A snake lay beneath the earth, in a deep hollow. There was no light there. It held the currents of the rivers in its teeth. Fame-from-the-Gods went down into the hollow. He carried fire in his hand. It saw the fire and was afraid. It let go of the currents and fled. But the hero followed it and killed it in the dark water. In the hollow lay the bones of many sheep. The rivers flowed up over the fields. Then the hero came up into the sun. His mother saw him and cried out with joy.

pie: kʷós dusménesm̥ h₁ógʷʰim péruni gʷʰn̥tóm? pérkʷunos tewh₂sós h₁ím h₂ḱm̥néh₁ kélh₂t. kʷós-ge wédōr déh₂nuh₂-kʷe spért? h₁uséwōm-ge déh₃tōr h₁íh₂ spért. h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ h₁ludʰéy ḱlutóm. nu h₁ím h₁erkʷóh₁ gʷr̥néHomes.
english: Who slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain? Perkwunos, the strong one, struck it with the stone. Who indeed freed the waters and the rivers? The giver of good things indeed freed them. His name is famous among the people. Now let us praise him with a hymn!

pie: póyḱos gʷṓs h₂epó h₂éǵet h₁íns-kʷe péruni wérǵt. gʷoldʰóh₁ h₁ésmi h₁n̥dóm HrudHént. bʰágos h₁éysōm wókʷn̥s ḱléwt. só h₁n̥gʷnís-kʷe ḱóm h₂én gʷh₂tā́m. h₁n̥gʷnís póyḱom h₁éwset ish₁rós-kʷe h₁íd swóh₁ h₂ḱm̥néh₁ skélHt. póyḱos bʰéwgt h₁n̥gʷnís h₁ím h₁r̥h₁pyét. léwkm̥ úd h₁n̥dʰént. poh₂iménes h₁íns h₂ml̥ǵént h₂mélǵos-kʷe sweh₂dú h₁ést.
english: An enemy drove the cows away and shut them up in a rock. Inside it they cried out with hunger. The god heard their voices. He and Fire went there together. Fire burned the enemy, and the strong one split the rock open with his stone. The enemy fled, but Fire seized him. They came out into the light. The shepherds milked them, and the milk was sweet.

pie: h₂éwsōs-ge diwés dʰugh₂tḗr gʷegʷóme. h₁léwdʰerons srówons h₂éǵrons-kʷe spéḱyeti. nu dusménēs dʰǵʰémi ḱéyor. bʰágom-ge gʷr̥nHté h₁yós h₁ím moréyet. nu ḱuh₁rṓy kéh₂nmn̥ gʷéHyete. nu nos h₂éwsōs h₁wésuh₂ bʰéroyh₁t.
english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, has indeed come. She sees the free streams and the fields. Now the ill-minded one lies on the earth. Praise the god indeed, who killed him! Now sing a song to the strong one! May Dawn bring us good things now!

pie: h₁és h₂yuHn̥ḱós h₂nḗr h₁suḱléwēs. ḱóymoy swéh₂h₁ méh₂tr̥h₁ ḱóm gʷíh₃wet h₁éḱwons-kʷe yéwgt. dusménēs ǵʰwḗr déh₂nuh₂ h₂ewlóy Hwért. wódr̥ pḱéwey ne h₁ést. h₁suḱléwēs ǵʰoysóm h₁épt h₂ewlóm-kʷe h₁r̥sḱét. h₁ím kʷéḱt gʰrémet-kʷe. h₂yuHn̥ḱós ne tréset Hyéh₁kt ǵʰoysóm. ǵʰoysós h₁ím h₂wégt ǵʰwḗr-kʷe mért. nu wiHrós h₂ewlóm Hrunépt. wédōr mélh₃t péḱu-kʷe péh₃t. méǵh₂ ḱléwos h₁suḱléwesm̥ gʷémt.
english: There was a young man, Of-Good-Fame. He lived in a village with his mother and yoked horses. An ill-minded beast had shut the rivers in a hollow. The livestock had no water. Of-Good-Fame seized a spear and went to the hollow. It saw him and roared. The youth did not tremble; he threw the spear. The spear pierced it, and the beast died. Then the hero broke open the hollow. The waters came forth, and the livestock drank. Great fame came to Of-Good-Fame.

english: I sing a new hymn to you. You indeed killed the serpent with the stone. Then you freed the waters for the people of the earth. Hear my song, Perkwunos! Give us livestock and swift horses now! Now guard our homes in the night!

english: When the god had slain the serpent, the people prepared a feast. They kindled a fire, cooked meat in a cauldron, and poured mead into cups. The young men sang a hymn about the beast. The god came and sat down at the feast. The old men told stories. He drank the mead and was glad. He gave them gifts: cattle and sheep. They said: "Giver of good things, be dear to us!"

english: At night a daughter asked her mother: "Tell me a story." The night was long, and the daughter listened. The mother told the story of the serpent. "A serpent lay in the waters and swallowed them. Men were thirsty, and the cattle died. Then a hero came, Of-Goodly-Fame. He struck the head of the serpent with a stone. The serpent died, and the water came forth." The daughter said: "I am not afraid of it." Her mother laughed and said: "It is dead. Sleep!"
